https://wiki.php.net/rfc/flexible_heredo.where: PHP RFC: Flexible Heredoc and Nowdoc Syntaxes (v0.9)
https://wiki.php.net/rfc/flexible_heredo.says: Lets the heredoc closing marker be indented and removes that marker's indentation from every line of the body, for PHP 7.3; no other language is cited.

https://openjdk.org/jeps/378.says: Defines Java text blocks, which drop incidental leading whitespace with the closing-delimiter line taken into account, and quotes Brian Goetz on requests to copy Swift's or Rust's multi-line literals; Perl is not mentioned.

https://openjdk.org/jeps/326.says: Surveys sixteen languages including Perl, lists Perl's qq{...} among delimiter styles, and describes heredocs as a Unix-shell device that spread to Perl and that many regard as outdated.

https://github.com/dotnet/csharplang/blo.says: Specifies triple-quote raw strings whose final line's indentation is removed from every content line, with mismatched indentation an error; the text names no other language, Swift and Perl included.

https://bugs.ruby-lang.org/issues/9098.says: Asks to bring Rails' String#strip_heredoc into the language; Avdi Grimm suggests the <<~ form, Matz accepts it in November 2015, and no reply in the thread mentions Perl or Raku.

https://marc.info/?l=groovy-dev&m=113684.where: groovy-dev, Re: Suggestions for improvement to Groovy
https://marc.info/?l=groovy-dev&m=113684.says: Argues Groovy should drop its ambiguous ... range operator and proposes ..<, <.. and <..< for exclusive bounds, with Ruby the only other language he brings up.

https://github.com/swiftlang/swift/blob/.who: Apple's Swift team, internal release notes
https://github.com/swiftlang/swift/blob/.says: Logs the half-open range moving to Ruby-style ... in February 2014, a swap in May, then the rename to ..< on 23 June, which the entry says Groovy and other languages already use.

https://appdevelopermagazine.com/apple-o.says: Reports that Xcode 6 beta 3 respelled Swift's half-open range as ..<, replacing .., so that it reads clearly beside the closed-range ... operator.

https://github.com/Kotlin/KEEP/blob/mast.where: Kotlin KEEP: Open-ended ranges and rangeUntil operator
https://github.com/Kotlin/KEEP/blob/mast.says: Its comparison of other languages' range operators covers Swift's ..<, Ruby's ..., Groovy's ..<, <.. and <..<, and Rust's ..=; Raku's caret forms are absent.

https://youtrack.jetbrains.com/issue/KT-.where: Kotlin YouTrack KT-15613, Introduce special syntax for the until operator
https://youtrack.jetbrains.com/issue/KT-.says: Requests a dedicated operator for Kotlin's until ranges and names Swift's ..< as the requester's preferred model.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rust-l.says: Proposes a...b for inclusive ranges and remarks that its .. versus ... split reverses Ruby's meaning exactly; Perl is not mentioned.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dotnet.says: Introduces ^n to index from the end and an end-exclusive .. range built on Index and Range types, without citing any other language.

https://github.com/apache/groovy/commit/.says: Gives closures an implicit single parameter named it, illustrated with findAll and map over a list; the commit names no source for the idea.

https://scala-lang.org/files/archive/spe.says: Lists implicit anonymous functions as new in 2.5: underscores in argument positions form a lambda, each underscore a separate parameter, with no source or rationale given.

https://github.com/swiftlang/swift/commi.says: Renames anonymous closure arguments from _0, _1 to $0, $1, the message recording that Bertrand favoured the dollar spelling; no reason or precedent is given.

https://downloads.ctfassets.net/oxjq45e8.where: Slides, Shoulders of Giants: Languages Kotlin learned from
https://downloads.ctfassets.net/oxjq45e8.says: Credits Groovy for Kotlin's implicit it parameter, attributes the null-safety operators (as?, !!, ?. and ?:) jointly to Groovy and C#, and on other slides credits Java, Scala, C# and Gosu.

https://bugs.ruby-lang.org/issues/4475.where: Ruby Feature #4475, default variable name for parameter
https://bugs.ruby-lang.org/issues/4475.says: Requests a default name for a block's parameter; the eight-year thread, closed in 2019 with numbered parameters, cites Elixir's &1 and Clojure's %1 but never Perl or Raku.

https://bugs.ruby-lang.org/issues/18980.who: Takashi Kokubun (k0kubun), Ruby committer; accepted by Matz
https://bugs.ruby-lang.org/issues/18980.says: Proposes it as a name for an unnamed block parameter, discusses Kotlin's it, and draws zverok's warning against adding Perlisms; Matz accepts it for Ruby 3.4 in December 2023.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rust-l.says: Credits Haskell's NamedFieldPuns and ES6 shorthand properties, and weighs a colon-prefixed S { :x } form, attributed to MoonScript, against confusion with Ruby and Elixir symbols.

https://bugs.ruby-lang.org/issues/14579.says: Proposes omitting a hash or keyword-argument value that matches a same-named variable; Matz first objects that it departs from ES6, accepts it in 2021, and Perl comes up only in objections to ES6-style braces.

https://peps.python.org/pep-0736/.who: Joshua Bambrick and Chris Angelico, PEP authors
https://peps.python.org/pep-0736/.where: PEP 736, Shorthand syntax for keyword arguments at invocation
https://peps.python.org/pep-0736/.says: Proposes f(x=) call-site punning; its prior-art survey covers the f-string x= form, Ruby, ReasonML, SystemVerilog, Jakt, OCaml, JavaScript and Rust, and Raku is not among them.
https://peps.python.org/pep-0736/.quote: Several modern languages provide similar features during function invocation, sometimes referred to as 'punning'.
https://peps.python.org/pep-0736/.rest: Before this the section cites Python's own f-string `f'{x=}'`. The list that follows gives Ruby, ReasonML, SystemVerilog and Jakt at the call site, then OCaml, JavaScript and Rust beyond it; Raku is not among them.

https://web.archive.org/web/201107020635.who: ECMAScript wiki strawman (TC39), last edited by Brendan Eich
https://web.archive.org/web/201107020635.says: Proposes abbreviating object literals whose property names equal variable names, mirroring the destructuring shorthand, and cites SpiderMonkey and Rhino already accepting {x, y} in JS 1.8.1.

https://peps.python.org/pep-3102/.says: Proposes parameters that can be filled only by keyword, declared after a varargs parameter or a bare star, and names no other language as a model.
https://peps.python.org/pep-3102/.quote: In particular, it enables the declaration of "keyword-only" arguments: arguments that can only be supplied by keyword and which will never be automatically filled in by a positional argument.
https://peps.python.org/pep-3102/.rest: They are declared after a varargs parameter, or after a bare `*` when the function takes no varargs. The PEP names no other language as a model.

https://peps.python.org/pep-0570/.who: Larry Hastings, Pablo Galindo, Mario Corchero and Eric Vander Weele, PEP authors
https://peps.python.org/pep-0570/.says: Proposes a / marker for positional-only parameters in Python 3.8 and names C alone as precedent, noting the slash already appeared for C-implemented functions.
https://peps.python.org/pep-0570/.quote: Users may be surprised when first encountering positional-only notation. This is expected given that it has only recently been documented and it is not possible to use in Python code. For these reasons, this notation is currently an outlier that appears only in CPython APIs developed in C.
https://peps.python.org/pep-0570/.rest: The PEP makes the `/` marker, until then a documentation convention for C-implemented functions such as `pow()`, usable in Python 3.8 code. It cites no other language.

https://pypi.org/project/plac/.says: Describes plac as deriving a script's command-line options from a function's signature; the earliest release listed, 0.3.0, was uploaded on 2 Jun 2010.

https://github.com/c-blake/cligen.says: Credits Andrey Mikhaylenko's argh, a Python library, as the model for cligen's approach of generating command lines from Nim procedure signatures.

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/archiv.says: Announces a revised C# 2.0 specification credited to Anders Hejlsberg, with nullable types as its largest new area, and tells a commenter no change list exists; no origin for ?? is given.

https://ecma-international.org/wp-conten.says: Standardises ?? as supplying a fallback for a null nullable value, usable with reference types too; Annex F, the bibliography, cites just C, C++, REXX and ISO 31-0.

https://github.com/swiftlang/swift/commi.who: Joe Groff, Swift compiler engineer at Apple
https://github.com/swiftlang/swift/commi.says: Adds ?? to the lexer and standard library, describing it only as resembling the null-defaulting operators of other languages, with no language named.

https://wiki.php.net/rfc/isset_ternary.who: Andrea Faulds, RFC author (patch by Nikita Popov)
https://wiki.php.net/rfc/isset_ternary.says: Proposes ?? for PHP 7, mentions C# only to say the precedence matches it, and contains neither a prior-art survey nor any reference to Perl.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tc39/p.who: Gabriel Isenberg, Daniel Ehrenberg and Daniel Rosenwasser, proposal authors
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tc39/p.says: Motivates ?? by the pitfalls of || defaults and gives a single prior-art link, to Wikipedia's article on the null coalescing operator.

https://github.com/dotnet/csharplang/blo.who: Cyrus Najmabadi, champion (C# language design team)
https://github.com/dotnet/csharplang/blo.says: Lists prior art for comparison chaining: CPL and BCPL, Icon as Python's inspiration, CoffeeScript and Raku, plus math-oriented Python, Julia and Mathematica and several variadic Lisps.
Approves chained relational comparison unchanged, singles out Python among math-oriented languages as its model, and ranks it fourth of five features for implementation; Raku is not mentioned.

https://github.com/brownplt/pyret-lang/w.where: pyret-lang wiki, design note TM017 Numbers
https://github.com/brownplt/pyret-lang/w.says: Sketches two separate number types for Pyret, exact arbitrary-precision rationals and approximations written with a tilde, with no automatic conversion between them; it mentions neither Perl nor Raku.

https://groovy-lang.org/syntax.html.where: Groovy Language Documentation, Syntax: decimal literals
https://groovy-lang.org/syntax.html.says: States that Groovy makes java.math.BigDecimal the default type of decimal literals, for exact decimal arithmetic; the page gives no precedent for the choice.

https://www.haskell.org/onlinereport/has.who: Haskell 2010 Language Report, ed. Simon Marlow
https://www.haskell.org/onlinereport/has.says: Specifies that a floating literal denotes fromRational applied to an exact Rational, so a literal such as 0.1 stands for an exact fraction before conversion.

https://github.com/scala/scala/pull/7540.says: Deprecates the Unicode arrows ⇒, ← and →, resolving scala-dev#585 and scala/bug#11210, with no reference to any other language.

https://groovy-lang.org/objectorientatio.where: Groovy Language Documentation, Object orientation: traits
https://groovy-lang.org/objectorientatio.says: Shows an existing object gaining traits at run time through as or withTraits, which return a new object rather than the original, and states no inspiration for the feature.

http://schemeworkshop.org/2006/13-siek.p.where: Gradual Typing for Functional Languages, Scheme and Functional Programming Workshop
http://schemeworkshop.org/2006/13-siek.p.says: Introduces gradual typing, crediting Thatte's quasi-static typing and citing Common Lisp, Dylan, Cecil, Boo, Bigloo and Strongtalk as related optional or partial typing; Perl is not mentioned.

https://peps.python.org/pep-0484/.who: Guido van Rossum, Jukka Lehtosalo and Łukasz Langa, PEP authors
https://peps.python.org/pep-0484/.says: Sets out Python's type-hint notation, saying it draws heavily on mypy and on the theory of gradual typing; no Perl design is cited.
https://peps.python.org/pep-0484/.quote: The proposal is strongly inspired by mypy. … The type system supports unions, generic types, and a special type named `Any` which is consistent with (i.e. assignable to and from) all types. This latter feature is taken from the idea of gradual typing.
https://peps.python.org/pep-0484/.rest: The lines left out show `Sequence[int]` as an example of the notation. Other approaches it borrowed from or compares itself with are left to PEP 482; Perl appears nowhere in PEP 484.

https://www.artima.com/weblogs/viewpost..where: Artima blog, The fate of reduce() in Python 3000
https://www.artima.com/weblogs/viewpost..says: Proposes short-circuiting any() and all() builtins, used with generator expressions, as replacements for most reduce() uses, and presents them as largely bringing back ABC's quantifiers.

https://github.com/swiftlang/swift/commi.says: Implements Swift string interpolation written as a backslash followed by a parenthesised expression, attributing the hardest pieces of the work to Doug Gregor.

https://lists.swift.org/pipermail/swift-.where: swift-evolution, thread on replacing the interpolation syntax
https://lists.swift.org/pipermail/swift-.says: Endorses Jordan Rose's account that \() reuses the string escape character, its parentheses once mirroring calls to String initialisers, and argues a replacement would force escaping another character such as $.

https://web.archive.org/web/201112231643.who: Mike Samuel's quasi-literal proposal, ECMAScript wiki (TC39)
https://web.archive.org/web/201112231643.says: Chooses backquotes because JavaScript leaves them unused while Perl, PHP, Ruby and Scheme already quote with them, takes ${...} from jQuery templates and PHP, and offers $ident matching Ruby, Bash, Perl and PHP.

https://peps.python.org/pep-0215/.says: Proposes $-prefixed string interpolation for Python, likening it to the way awk, Perl, Tcl and Unix shells substitute variables into strings.
https://peps.python.org/pep-0215/.quote: This document proposes a string interpolation feature for Python to allow easier string formatting. The suggested syntax change is the introduction of a '$' prefix that triggers the special interpretation of the '$' character within a string, in a manner reminiscent to the variable interpolation found in Unix shells, awk, Perl, or Tcl.

https://peps.python.org/pep-0498/.says: Introduces f-strings for Python 3.6; its section on other languages names none and simply refers readers to Wikipedia's survey of string interpolation.
https://peps.python.org/pep-0498/.quote: Wikipedia has a good discussion of string interpolation in other programming languages. This feature is implemented in many languages, with a variety of syntaxes and restrictions.
https://peps.python.org/pep-0498/.rest: That is the whole of the section headed “Similar support in other languages”; it names none of them.

https://www.open-std.org/jtc1/sc22/wg21/.says: Proposes C++'s <=> with typed ordering results, lists Perl's <=> among existing three-way comparisons, and claims Haskell is the sole major language whose comparison returns an enumeration.

https://www.perl.com/pub/2001/05/03/wall.says: Ruling on RFC 162, Wall picks option (e): each heredoc line loses as much leading whitespace as the terminator carries, counting hard tabs as eight spaces when guessing.

https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/issues/.says: Offers C# a heredoc idea explicitly taken from Perl 6's quoting docs: a caret-prefixed string whose user-chosen terminator ends a body starting on the next line.

https://github.com/Perl/perl5/commit/cdd.where: Perl/perl5 commit cdd6375, Add indented here-docs
https://github.com/Perl/perl5/commit/cdd.says: Adds <<~ heredocs whose closing delimiter may be indented, strips that delimiter's leading whitespace from each line, and makes lines lacking it fatal; the commit credits no source.

https://www.nntp.perl.org/group/perl.per.says: Opens the thread with a rough patch for indented heredocs and suggests stripping could follow Perl 6's rules, which he summarises: deeper lines keep their extra indent, shallower ones warn.
Answering Aristotle Pagaltzis's request for the bash and zsh <<- spelling, says he is open to either and based his version loosely on Ruby 2.3's <<~.

https://github.com/Perl/perl5/blob/blead.says: Lists the here-doc indentation-mismatch message under class (F), a fatal error, rather than as a warning.

https://web.archive.org/web/200512201435.who: John Rose, Groovy JSR grammar notes
https://web.archive.org/web/200512201435.says: Records the switch of right-exclusive range syntax to x..<y, keeping the older x...y legal for a transition period.

https://github.com/dotnet/csharplang/iss.says: Tells commenters that what the caret means in Perl, regular expressions or Fortran has no bearing on the C# design.

https://bugs.ruby-lang.org/issues/12133.where: Ruby Feature #12133, Ability to exclude start when defining a range
https://bugs.ruby-lang.org/issues/12133.says: Responding to a request for ranges that exclude their start, asks whether Perl 6's neko operator (^..) would serve; Matz does not comment and the ticket is closed unimplemented.

https://github.com/dart-lang/language/is.where: dart-lang/language issue #2105 (Ranges in switch cases), comment
https://github.com/dart-lang/language/is.says: Surveys range spellings in Perl, Raku (all four caret forms), Ruby, Swift and Rust, then prefers C#-style relational patterns and leans toward deferring range syntax.

https://github.com/ziglang/zig/issues/35.says: Proposes Raku-style carets for Zig switch ranges, such as 0 ..^ 5 or 10 ^..^ 15, linking Raku's Range docs; the issue was closed in January 2021 without adopting them.

https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues.says: Objects to spelling Rust's inclusive range ..^ because Perl 6 already uses that operator to mean exclusive, the reverse of the proposal.

https://github.com/swiftlang/swift/commi.says: Implements anonymous closure arguments for the language that became Swift, spelled _0, _1 and so on, eleven days after Lattner's initial commit in the public repository.

https://oleb.net/2019/chris-lattner-swif.says: Lattner recounts that Swift's 2010 design work began at a whiteboard with Bertrand Serlet, who then ran Apple's software organisation.

https://github.com/scala/scala/tree/v2.5.where: Commit history up to the v2.5.0 tag
https://github.com/scala/scala/tree/v2.5.says: Across the 7,148 commits up to the tag, no message mentions underscore placeholders or where they came from, and Odersky's early-2007 messages give no rationale.

https://bugs.ruby-lang.org/issues/15723.who: Stefan Schüßler (proposer); Benoit Daloze, Ruby core committer
https://bugs.ruby-lang.org/issues/15723.says: Argues numbered block parameters make code harder to read and recalls Ruby already discourages Perl-style $ variables; Benoit Daloze later says he does not want Ruby's readability sliding toward Perl's.

https://mail.python.org/pipermail/python.says: Dismisses proposed bracket notation for special parameter lists, telling the list that Python should not be copying Perl 6; no one in the thread had brought up Perl 6 before.
Pronounces that a bare * in a parameter list makes the parameters after it keyword-only, to head off further unusual notations.
Posts the draft PEP 3102 to python-dev, opening a 62-message thread in which no other language, Perl included, is named as a precedent.

https://www.nntp.perl.org/group/perl.per.says: Adds S06's MAIN section: Unix-style switches map to MAIN's named parameters, multi MAIN candidates dispatch, a dispatch failure invokes USAGE or a generated message, and the direct-run rule is compared with Perl 5's unless caller.

https://bugs.ruby-lang.org/issues/5011#n.who: Yusuke Endoh (mame), relaying the Ruby developer meeting
https://bugs.ruby-lang.org/issues/5011#n.says: Reports that the 21 July developer meeting rejected the Perl 6-like main proposal; Matz felt improving optparse was worthwhile but this proposal pointed the wrong way.

https://github.com/golang/go/issues/1717.says: A user asks for main() parameters bound to command-line arguments as in Perl 6, citing the 2010 Advent post; Fitzpatrick closes it within the hour, saying Go 2 will not take every language's features.

https://jsiek.github.io/home/WhatIsGradu.says: Names Dylan, Cecil, Common Lisp and others as having optional annotations, and lists Perl 6 with Python 3k and ECMAScript 4 among new languages that gradual typing aims to underpin.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gradual_ty.says: Claims, with no footnote, that Raku supported gradual typing from its beginning, and credits Siek and Taha with naming and developing the idea in 2006.
